key_insight: Stern-sculling propulsion relies mainly on lift during lateral strokes and added-mass effects during backward strokes, with peak efficiency near 65% at intermediate boat speed.
engineering_relevance: The findings can inform oscillating-oar propulsion design and operating speeds for efficient human-powered boats.
method: Continuously measure oar kinematics and boat motion.
Measure forces acting on the oar across a broad range of boat speeds.
Determine propulsive efficiency as a function of boat speed.
evidence_signal: Measurements show efficiency peaking at approximately 65% at intermediate speed and declining to approximately 25% at higher speeds.
watch_item: The abstract reports experimental measurements, not an AI or CFD surrogate, and does not establish generalizability across oar geometries or boat designs.
paper_title: Hydrodynamics and propulsive efficiency of stern-sculling propulsion
